reason: E1 supports that severe localized lattice distortion from interstitial/large atoms creates strain fields and alters dislocation behavior, but it does not address ion irradiation or multilayer systems. E2 shows that interfacial lattice misfit affects creep resistance in Ni-based superalloys, but this is a different material system and mechanism (impeding dislocations) than the proposed heterogeneous activation. The specific claim that ion irradiation can be used to controllably introduce such distortions in HEA multilayers is unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Localized lattice distortions in HEAs can be induced by interstitial or large substitutional atoms, creating strain fields that alter dislocation behavior.
These strain fields can promote cross-slip and change the plastic deformation mechanism.
Lattice misfit at interfaces generates stress fields that influence dislocation motion and creep resistance.
Controlled ion irradiation can introduce tunable, localized strain fields in a multilayer without destroying its integrity.
